transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (Sentinel Head of ML), Ben Clarke (Platform Eng), Rosa Martinez (SRE), Tom Ellis (Product)

Summary: Quarterly business review + ongoing health check. Focus on usage trends, cost optimization opportunities (batching/quantization), recent reliability incidents and mitigations, security/compliance questions (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs), and roadmap alignment for a potential Dedicated pilot.

Topics: Usage & cost, Reliability incidents and SLOs, Private/Dedicated deployment tradeoffs, Roadmap & next steps, Security/compliance docs.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call — who we got from Sentinel?
[00:10] Aisha: Hi Jordan, Aisha here. Ben, Rosa, Tom on my side.
[00:14] Ben: Yep Ben here.
[00:18] Rosa: Rosa.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. I'll let Miguel do a one-line QBR framing then Priya will cover reliability/perf stuff. Miguel?
[00:25] Miguel: Hey everyone, thanks. Quick QBR: usage has grown ~28% q/q, costs up ~18% due to longer sequences and increased p99 retries, we want to review where Redwood can help with batching and cache to bring unit economics down. Also go over the April incident mitigation and next steps for pilot.
[00:44] Aisha: Sounds good. We definitely saw more long-context calls after the product change. Our team is sensitive to p95/p99 latency and cost budgets.
[00:54] Priya: Great, I'll start with the perf snapshot — apologies if some of the model names get munged, the transcripter sometimes says "Red wood" or KV chache, sorry.
[01:04] Priya: So last 90 days usage: 2.1B tokens generated, 320M embedding units, 70% of requests under 2s but the tail is rough — p95 around 3.8s, p99 around 7.2s for the high-context flows. We saw a plateau after adding prefix caching but there are still cold-start hits on new sessions.
[01:28] Ben: Can you break down by hosted vs Dedicated sim? We're still evaluating which path for pilot.
[01:33] Miguel: They've been on hosted with a reserved throughput commitment, no Dedicated yet.
[01:38] Priya: Correct, current is hosted API with some routed requests to higher tiers. For Dedicated pilot we can pencil in 4 cards (GPUs) to start with autoscale. Our notes show a ~30% unit cost reduction when we enable quantized kernels + KV caching for your workload mix.
[01:56] Aisha: 30% is great — what's the tradeoff in accuracy / hallucination?
[02:01] Priya: Minimal in our tests; for some sensitive instr prompts we recommend 8-bit quantization with monitoring. We'll also run A/B on your golden prompts. There's a short risk window but the eval harness picks regressions.
[02:16] Rosa: On reliability — last month we had a 45m blip that affected a small percentage of production requests. Can someone summarize root cause?
[02:24] Jordan: Sure, I'll give the quick version, Priya can add details. It was an autoscaler misconfiguration that didn't account for our cache warm-up profile. Traffic spiked and new nodes got provisioned but cold KV caches caused p99 spikes and our fallback to a smaller model wasn't triggered fast enough.
[02:44] Priya: Yes, internal tracing showed KV cache warm up at node spin-up was the dominant factor. We pushed a fix to the autoscaler policy to pre-warm small prefix caches and lowered the threshold for canary rollback. That reduced similar incidents in our staging runs.
[03:00] Ben: Any mitigation we should have on our side? We use relatively bursty traffic.
[03:06] Priya: A couple options: consistent prefix caching for common session starters, adopt a short-tailed retry with jitter, and possibly run a thin Dedicated pool so burst traffic can land without spin-up. Also, set SLOs for p95 vs p99 and have canary fallback rules tuned to your traffic patterns.
[03:24] Aisha: Cost question — does Dedicated add predictable cost but higher committed spend? We want to make sure we don't overcommit.
[03:30] Jordan: Yes Dedicated is reserved capacity — commit to a monthly baseline. That lets you get better unit economics with dedicated GPUs, but you pay for reserved capacity. We can structure a pilot with a smaller commitment and burst options. I'll send models of committed vs burst pricing.
[03:46] Tom: What's the timeline for moving to Private/VPC? We have regulatory requirements that might push us to private next year.
[03:52] Miguel: We support Private deployments with a customer-managed VPC or on-prem bundles. The path usually: start with Hosted, then a Dedicated pilot, then pivot to Private if compliance requires. Each step has checklist items: IAM, SSO, KMS integration, and audit log forwarding.
[04:10] Rosa: On KMS — we need to know if keys can stay in our HSM and whether Redwood can support bring-your-own-key.
[04:16] Priya: Yes, BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated via KMS integration; for Hosted we provide envelope encryption with customer-managed CMKs in many clouds — but we'll check specifics for your HSM vendor.
[04:28] Aisha: Can you also confirm retention windows for logs and models? We need at least 1 year of audit logs retained and ability to disable retention for certain PII flows.
[04:36] Miguel: We'll share our retention matrix; short answer is yes for 1 year retention and we have controls for redaction/PII scrubbing on ingest. I'll attach the doc.
[04:48] Jordan: Let's pivot to the roadmap — Sentinel's product team shared a plan to expand context to 50k tokens next year. That changes perf and cost profile. Priya, what does that imply?
[04:58] Priya: Longer contexts increase KV cache size and memory pressure. Kernel selection matters; we'd suggest progressive rollout with model shards that support longer contexts and enable streaming to reduce p95 latency. Quantization will help but you may need more GPU RAM or model parallel configs. We can run a cost simulation.
[05:17] Ben: If we need 50k in production, are there recommended model variants?
[05:21] Priya: We recommend model-X-long or our Redwood-verified long-context forks. We'll run evals on your prompt set to pick the best tradeoff. Also, consider chunked embeddings for search to lower tokenization costs.
[05:34] Tom: Any security review items to surface to our compliance team?
[05:38] Miguel: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO if needed, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, and we have a data processing agreement for EU data residency. I'll attach certs and the short security briefing.
[05:52] Aisha: On the pilot — what success metrics should we track? Cost per 1k useful tokens, p95 latency < 3s, and error rate < 0.1% maybe?
[06:02] Priya: Those are good. I'd also add model accuracy on golden prompts (no regressions), and cold-start p99 under an agreed threshold. We'll propose an experiment design.
[06:12] Jordan: Okay let's capture next steps — I'll send pricing and dedicated options, Miguel will send SOC2 artifacts, Priya sets up perf test. Any objections?
[06:21] Rosa: None. Just one more ask: can we get an artifact showing previous incident timeline and mitigations?
[06:26] Priya: Yes I'll export the incident timeline and what config changed.
[06:30] Ben: If you can also include sample terraform or k8s snippets for the Dedicated provision that would help our infra team.
[06:36] Jordan: We'll include a short infra snippet and a link to the Dedicated quickstart repo.
[06:40] Aisha: Thanks — this was helpful.
[06:42] Jordan: Great — wrap up: agreed actions and we'll reconvene after the perf run. Thanks everyone.
